claims.action: traced the Yellow River source after the mission to Daxia

claims.assessment: After Zhang Qian's mission to Daxia traced the river source, the so-called Kunlun of the Basic Annals of Yu cannot be verified; the Documents are nearer the truth on the nine provinces' mountains and rivers, while the Basic Annals of Yu and the Classic of Mountains are reckless fancy.

claims.statement: Historian's zan uses Zhang Qian's mission to Daxia and tracing of the river source to reject the Kunlun claims of the Basic Annals of Yu and the Classic of Mountains.

translationRepairs: Volume 61: Biographies the Thirty-first, Zhang Qian and Li Guangli.
Volume 61: Biography Thirty-first, Zhang Qian and Li Guangli.
傳第三十一 is the standard ordinal biography title; “Biographies the Thirty-first” is ungrammatical, and “Biography Thirty-first” correctly renders the Chinese without inventing content.
This unit is only 孫猛, kinship plus given name; “Zhang Meng” invents the surname 張 not present here (s0130’s 騫孫猛 confirms grandson Meng, not a written 張).
Literal must track 孫猛 alone; inserting Zhang invents a surname absent from this unit, while “Grandson Meng” matches the Chinese.
Eleven years later, in Zhenghe 3 (90 BCE), Ershi took seventy thousand horse out of Wuyuan against the Xiongnu and crossed the Zhiju River.
Eleven years later, in Zhenghe 3 (90 BCE), Ershi led seventy thousand cavalry out of Wuyuan against the Xiongnu and crossed the Zhiju River.
將七萬騎 means he led seventy thousand cavalry; “took seventy thousand horse” is ungrammatical and weakens the command sense already clear in the Chinese.
